title: Traffic sculpting: version pinning with multi-tier fallbacks and canary splits
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Goal: Define and validate a product-level policy for how model version pinning (per-session or per-customer) interacts with region selection and tier routing (hosted/dedicated/private), while supporting canary / A-B rollouts and automated fallback to quantized or smaller model variants.

Background: We currently have separate mechanisms for region affinity, tier-based routing (geo -> tier -> model), and simple version pinning. This ticket is to unify the ordering/precedence and make expected behaviors explicit for product teams and SREs.

Key scenarios to handle (non-exhaustive):
- Customer pins model v2 for their workspace; some requests originate from eu-west while dedicated capacity for v2 is only in us-west. Decide routing: honor workspace pin and route cross-region; or route to nearest region with compatible variant and mark as degraded.
- Canary rollout: 10% of traffic should go to v3 canary for a cohort, but session-pin TTL should be respected so users routed to canary stay on it for TTL window.
- Tier degrade: if customer is on Dedicated tier but Dedicated pool for v3 is exhausted, fallback to Hosted v3 if allowed by customer policy; otherwise fallback to v2 in Dedicated or a quantized v3-hosted variant.
- Edge-case: user-level sticky affinity combined with geo-based emergency failover (region outage) needs deterministic override semantics.

Product decisions proposed:
1) Precedence order: explicit customer pin > session sticky pin (TTL) > policy-based routing (region/tier) > probabilistic canary sampling. Pins can be scoped: session, workspace, account. Workspace pins override session pins.
2) Cross-region routing: default is prefer same region; if pinned model not available in region, consult a compatibility matrix and fall back to the nearest compatible variant based on policy (prefer same tier, then compatible quantized variant, then cross-region exact-match). Cross-region routing requires an explicit billing and data-access opt-in; otherwise prefer local degrade.
3) Tier fallback: preserve customer tier where possible (Dedicated -> Hosted fallback only if customer allows cross-tier degrade). Offer opt-in policy per workspace for aggressive fallbacks to maintain latency.
4) Canary/A-B interaction: cohort selection happens at request arrival; once a session is sampled into a cohort, the session receives a pin for TTL seconds to ensure consistent model during an evaluation window.
5) Observability & gates: every fallback path increments a labeled metric and shows in Console under route-quality dashboard; canary cohorts expose compare charts for latency, perplexity/quality, and cost.

Acceptance criteria:
- Product config UI wireframes for per-workspace pinning scope and fallback policy controls (opt-in toggles and defaults).
- API contract documented for "pin_scope", "pin_ttl", and "allow_cross_tier_fallback" fields.
- Clear precedence doc with 6 worked examples + expected routing outcomes.
- Telemetry plan: metrics and dashboards for pin-hit-rate, fallback-rate by region/tier, canary cohort split accuracy, and cross-region cost delta.
- Rollout plan: staged rollout to internal customers, then opt-in beta, then default-on with safe thresholds.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Strict pin-first behavior improves predictability but may increase cross-region egress and cost. Alternative is to honor region first and mark pin as "best-effort".
- How aggressively do we allow cross-tier fallbacks for Dedicated customers? Conservative default vs aggressive default.
- TTL default for session pins (current proposals: 30m, 2h, session-length). Needs telemetry to pick.

Deliverables:
- PRD (link below), API spec, Console UX mocks, observability dashboard queries, and acceptance tests.
